message.reasoning_content:
Key suspicion: split-K coverage of K dimension. tiles = cdiv(cdiv(k,32), split_k). Then inner = (split*TILES+tile)*BK+lane covering split*TILES*BK range = cdiv(k,32)*BK >= K, masked. Good—covers all K when tiles*split*32 >= cdiv(k,32)*32 >= K. OK.

But when split_k=1, work dtype is fp16? No: work_dtype = fp32 when split_k==1. Fine. Actually when split_k>1, work dtype = fp16 (a.dtype). Partials stored as fp16 — intermediate rounding but tolerance is 0.01+0.001|target|; fp16 rounding of partials magnitude ≤128 → rounding up to ~0.0625 per split, 8 splits → up to 0.5 error? That could violate tolerance. Partial magnitudes: sum of products, each |a|,|b|≤0.5 → products ≤0.25, up to 512*... Actually largest partial magnitude bounded by 128 per contract. FP16 ulp at 128 is 0.0625. Split into 8 partials, each rounded to fp16 with error up to ulp/2 = 0.03125 each → total 0.25 error possibly exceeding 0.01 tolerance. Also accumulation of products in tl.dot with fp16 inputs — fp32 accumulate, fine.

Also tl.store(WORK + offset, accum) with work fp16 — accum fp32 stored to fp16 (Triton auto-converts). This is the classic planted bug. Also, for split_k>1, partials may exceed fp16 range? Bounded 128 fine.

Also BK=32 with tl.dot requires dims ≥16 — 16x16x32 ok.

Another: TILES = cdiv(cdiv(k,32), split_k); if k small, e.g., k=1: cdiv(1,32)=1, split=8 → tiles=1, splits cover lanes 0..7*32+... 8*32=256 > K, masked fine. But wait with split=8 and tiles=1, inner = split*1*32.. covers splits 0-7 each one tile of 32 → covers 0..255, masked to K. Fine.

Potential main bug: fp16 partial storage precision. Run probe testing tolerance across shapes/splits.
